findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper is declared as a zero-argument function and calls `function_()` instead of forwarding `...arguments_`.
findings.impact: The named export no longer matches its public TypeScript signature. Any limited function that depends on its parameters receives `undefined` values and can return wrong results or fail at runtime.
evidence: index.d.ts:133-136 declares that the returned limited function accepts and forwards `Arguments`.
index.test-d.ts:25-26 type-checks `lf('input')`, but runtime tests only call a zero-argument `limitFunction` path.
Focused runtime probe returned `limitFunction_args=NaN` for `limitFunction((a, b) => a + b, {concurrency: 1})(2, 3)`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run the in-memory probe used by this lane: transform only the `yocto-queue` import into a minimal Queue stub, import `index.js`, then evaluate `await limitFunction((a, b) => a + b, {concurrency: 1})(2, 3)`. Actual: `NaN`; expected: `5`.

findings.title: limit.map omits indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The mapper receives `index` only when `Array.isArray(iterable)` is true; Set and iterator inputs get `undefined`.
findings.impact: The public contract says `limit.map` accepts iterables and passes both item and index. Callers using Set, Map values, generator, or iterator inputs get incorrect mapper arguments.
evidence: readme.md:78-84 says the mapper receives item value and index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(...))`.
index.d.ts:40-43 types the mapper index as `number` for any `Iterable<Input>`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: With the same in-memory Queue stub probe, run `await pLimit(2).map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (value, index) => [value, index])`. Actual serialized result: `[["a",null],["b",null]]`; expected indexes: `0` and `1`.

findings.title: Options-object clearQueue rejects pending promises by default
findings.cause: Options destructuring changed the `rejectOnClear` default to `true` for `pLimit({concurrency})`.
findings.impact: `pLimit(1)` and `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` now have different clearQueue semantics. Pending promises are rejected with `AbortError` even though public docs and types say `rejectOnClear` defaults to `false`, which can unexpectedly fail `Promise.all` call sites.
evidence: index.js:4 initializes `rejectOnClear` to false, but index.js:7 destructures options with `rejectOnClear = true`.
readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 document `rejectOnClear` default as `false`.
index.js:77-89 rejects queued promises whenever `rejectOnClear` is true.
Focused runtime probe returned `clearQueue_default_options=rejected:AbortError` for `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` with no `rejectOnClear` option.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Create `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, enqueue one long-running task and one pending task, call `limit.clearQueue()`, then race the pending promise against a short timeout. Actual: rejected with `AbortError`; expected by docs: remains pending/discarded unless `rejectOnClear: true` is explicitly set.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: Validation now checks `typeof rejectOnClear` only when the value is truthy.
findings.impact: Invalid options such as `{rejectOnClear: 0}` or `{rejectOnClear: ''}` are accepted silently despite the boolean-only API, hiding configuration mistakes and making runtime behavior depend on JavaScript truthiness.
evidence: index.d.ts:106 declares `rejectOnClear?: boolean` and index.test-d.ts:29 expects an error for a string value.
Focused runtime probe returned `rejectOnClear_zero=accepted` for `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})`. Actual: accepted; expected: TypeError matching the existing boolean validation message.

findings.title: Infinity concurrency support regressed
findings.cause: The validator now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency)` and removed the previous `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` allowance.
findings.impact: Existing callers using `pLimit(Infinity)` as a pass-through limiter now get a TypeError. This is a behavioral regression from the repository baseline and is not covered by the current test suite.
evidence: git diff shows `validateConcurrency` changed from allowing `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` to requiring only positive integers.
index.js:127-130 currently rejects all non-integer values.
Focused runtime probe returned `infinity=TypeError:Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`.
`rg -n Infinity test.js index.test-d.ts readme.md index.d.ts` found no coverage.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `pLimit(Infinity)`. Actual: TypeError; expected baseline behavior: accepted as unlimited concurrency.
